name: Ignis-Perpetua
specific_features: Lava fountains reaching kilometers in height
description: Ignis-Perpetua burns with an inner fire that has never once dimmed in the span of recorded observation, its surface a hellscape of continent-scale lava lakes and pyroclastic flows that reshape the terrain on timescales measured in hours rather than epochs. The lava lakes glow with such intensity that the planet appears to have its own luminosity when viewed from the dark side, a smoldering ember against the black of space. Volcanic glass spires rise from cooled margins only to be consumed again as the lava levels shift.

The toxic atmosphere is a superheated mixture of sulfur compounds and carbon dioxide that would dissolve organic tissue on contact, its upper layers perpetually churned by electromagnetic storms generated by the vast quantities of charged particulates ejected by continuous eruptions. Visibility at surface level varies from a few hundred meters to near zero during major eruption events, the sky an oppressive ceiling of red-lit ash clouds punctuated by the blue-white arcs of volcanic lightning. Even hardened environmental suits have operational windows measured in single-digit hours.

The planet's extreme volcanism results from tidal heating by a nearby gas giant, a gravitational interaction that flexes the rocky body continuously and prevents its interior from ever cooling. This makes Ignis-Perpetua a geological laboratory without parallel, a world where processes that take millions of years on stable planets play out in real time. Research stations in high orbit study the eruption patterns and have identified cyclic behaviors that correlate with orbital mechanics, allowing rough prediction of the most violent episodes.

Commercial interest centers on the rare metals concentrated in the volcanic emissions, elements brought to the surface from deep within the planetary mantle by the relentless eruption cycle. Automated collection drones operating on the cooled margins of lava lakes have proven marginally profitable, though the attrition rate on equipment is staggering. Each lost drone must be written off completely, as recovery from active lava flows is impossible. The planet endures as a testament to the proposition that some resources are barely worth the cost of obtaining them.
